baseline_models.reading: He created the human from ʿalaq: bodily originating from clotted or adhering generative material.

focus_anchor.role: The verb makes the human its object and min introduces the material or originating condition.

activation_trace.role: Originating a thing, including bringing one thing into being from another, fits the verb and min construction.
The human-person or human-group scope supports generic humanity.
Thick or congealed blood and its piece provide the ordinary material sense; the paired leech scope supplies an attachment image, not a separate assertion of animal ancestry.
Conception taking hold supports a generative setting for the material image.

baseline_models.mechanism: A formed human is traced back through min to a materially different beginning. The supplied blood and conception scopes converge on bodily generation.
baseline_models.reader_inference: The text supplies creation, humanity, and origin from ʿalaq; the inventory supplies the blood, leech, and conception scopes. Identifying this as a generative beginning connects those elements. The isolated focus leaves the implicit subject unnamed; it does not specify an anatomical stage or distinguish collective material from plural units.
baseline_models.containment: Keep the ordinary creation reading primary. Do not turn the inventory's leech example into a literal claim or use the verse to assert modern embryological precision.

baseline_models.reading: The human's beginning carries an image of attachment: existence emerges from something that takes hold of or depends on another.

focus_anchor.role: The source phrase can retain the attaching image within its ordinary generative sense.

activation_trace.role: Clinging or hanging on another provides the relational image.
Conception taking hold connects physical attachment to the creation construction.

baseline_models.mechanism: The ordinary material origin also has a relational contour: what begins by taking hold is not pictured as independently established.
baseline_models.reader_inference: Attachment and conception are supplied scopes; interpreting attachment as dependence is my abstraction. A purely material reading remains sufficient, and the focus alone does not make an explicit moral argument.
baseline_models.containment: Describe a possible image of dependence, not a replacement translation of ʿalaq as relationships or a claim that every inventory sense operates here.

context_deltas.reading: Human generation specifies the creative work of the addressed person's Lord, making this origin personally relevant to the command to read.

focus_anchor.role: The repeated creation verb supplies a particular object for the preceding creative description.

activation_trace.role: Lordship identifies the authority to which creation belongs.
Nurture and completion stage by stage permit a caring, developmental resonance alongside authority.

structural_cues.role: Reading is commanded in the name of your Lord, characterized by creation.
Immediate verbal repetition identifies the creator and specifies humanity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Adjacent repetition resolves the implicit subject and moves from creation without an expressed object to human creation; the possessive address connects that general human origin to the reader.

changed_reading.before: An unnamed subject brings the human into being from ʿalaq.
changed_reading.after: The creator is your Lord, whose human-making work grounds the surrounding summons to read and may resonate with nurture.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The subject link and personal address follow directly from syntax. Treating creation as grounding the command is a discourse inference; nurture is a compatible supplied resonance, not the only meaning of rabb.
context_deltas.containment: Do not derive a full developmental timetable or identify the addressee through external biography.

context_deltas.reading: The human formed from ʿalaq is also the recipient of knowledge: bodily creation begins a trajectory of bestowed capacity rather than fixing humanity at its initial material condition.

focus_anchor.role: The created human is repeated as the taught human.

structural_cues.role: Creation gives humanity a received bodily beginning.
The repeated command and superlative generosity frame what follows as bestowal.
The Lord's teaching includes the pen as a medium.
The repeated direct object links the human made to the human taught, explicitly contrasting prior not-knowing.

context_deltas.mechanism: Parallel transitive clauses assign the same human object to creation and teaching. Initial material and initial ignorance become two conditions from which the Lord enables a new capacity.

changed_reading.before: The focus tells where human bodily existence begins.
changed_reading.after: That origin is the first part of a creation-and-teaching account in which the human becomes capable of receiving and transmitting knowledge.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The repeated object and teaching by the pen are textual. The trajectory and extension to transmission are my synthesis of their sequence and the pen; the verses need not narrate a precise chronological course for an individual.
context_deltas.containment: Preserve both modest origin and subsequent endowment. Avoid treating the origin as proof of intrinsic worthlessness or equating biological formation with literacy.

context_deltas.reading: Origin from ʿalaq becomes a corrective to the human's view of himself as self-sufficient, while return to the Lord prevents that dependence from being confined to the past.

focus_anchor.role: Received existence and material origin stand against the later assessment of independence.

activation_trace.role: Wealth and lack of need are both within scope; the contrast need not reduce self-sufficiency to money alone.

structural_cues.role: The generic human is created from a prior material condition.
The same human designation recurs with emphatic transgression.
The transgression is connected to a self-assessment of sufficiency.
Return to the Lord supplies a destination that the claimed independence cannot annul.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repetition of humanity across creation, teaching, and transgression turns the origin into counterevidence to self-sufficiency. Origin and return frame the intervening self-assessment within an enduring relation to the Lord.

changed_reading.before: Humanity has a materially dependent beginning, possibly evoking attachment.
changed_reading.after: That beginning participates in a sustained rebuttal of imagined independence, extending from received existence to unavoidable return.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The cause-like connection in 96:7 and return in 96:8 are supplied text. Reading 96:2 as their retrospective corrective is a discourse inference. Material wealth remains a live narrower sense of sufficiency; no attachment branch is required for the basic contrast.
context_deltas.containment: Do not say material generation causes transgression, or that the generic declaration condemns every human action.

context_deltas.reading: The common created human condition limits a person's claim to control another person's worship; the assembled supporters later invoked cannot confer the Creator's authority.

focus_anchor.role: Generic humanity can encompass both the prohibiting person and the worshipping servant.

structural_cues.role: The human category shares a created origin.
A person exercises prohibiting power.
The prohibition targets a servant at prayer.
The opponent's claimed strength is socially supported by his assembly.
The answering summons exposes a superior counterforce.
The addressee is explicitly released from obedience to the prohibitor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The generic created human becomes a shared category across a conflict between humans. The later refusal of obedience prevents created dependence from licensing submission to every human claimant of power.

changed_reading.before: The focus describes humanity's common origin without an explicit interpersonal consequence.
changed_reading.after: In the worship conflict, that common origin can undercut the prohibitor's presumption of supreme authority and his reliance on a social following.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The conflict, assembly, and refusal are textual. Their grounding in common creation is my relational inference; the passage can oppose this particular prohibition without announcing a general theory of social equality.
context_deltas.containment: Present a local challenge to arrogated authority, not a comprehensive political doctrine or an identification of historical actors.

context_deltas.reading: The body originating from ʿalaq remains subject to the Lord: the later contrast between a seized forelock and voluntary prostration offers two ways that embodied dependence becomes manifest.

focus_anchor.role: Bodily creation provides the embodied human whose head is later seized or lowered.

activation_trace.role: Taking the forelock includes coercive humiliation.
Humble prostration includes putting the forehead on the ground, supplying a bodily contrast to seizure.

structural_cues.role: Human bodily origin anchors the comparison.
The warning places the bodily person under coercive control.
Moral attributes are attached metonymically to the bodily forelock.
The concluding command joins voluntary bodily lowering to nearness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The material human of the focus becomes the morally acting, bodily vulnerable human of the conclusion. Forced seizure and chosen lowering give opposing enactments of creaturely dependence.

changed_reading.before: The body's dependence belongs to its origin.
changed_reading.after: The created body remains the site of accountability and can enact acknowledged dependence through prostration and approach.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The forelock warning and prostration command are supplied; their pairing as two enactments of created dependence is my synthesis. They concern distinct discourse roles, not a claim that one individual performs both actions.
context_deltas.containment: Do not infer neuroscience from the forelock's moral adjectives or treat prostration as a biological consequence of embryonic attachment.

surprising_valid_outliers.reading: The command to read can carry a faint generative echo around creation from ʿalaq: the read-root's womb-enclosing image makes receiving and bringing forth a secondary analogy for learning.

focus_anchor.role: The ordinary generative source provides the bodily pole of the analogy.

activation_trace.role: The supplied womb-enclosing placenta, fetus, or pregnancy scope, especially in camel expressions, resonates with the focus's generation image.
Conception taking hold is the focus-side lexical bridge.

structural_cues.role: The reading imperative immediately precedes the creation statement.
Generation intervenes between repeated commands to read.
The repeated imperative brackets the generative statement.
Teaching supplies the cognitive counterpart to bodily coming-into-being.

surprising_valid_outliers.mechanism: A branch-distant reproductive image in the surrounding reading root meets an explicit reproductive origin in the focus, permitting an analogy between generation and the emergence of knowledge.

changed_reading.before: Generation and reading are linked by adjacent creation and teaching statements.
changed_reading.after: They may also resonate through an inventory-supplied image of enclosing pregnancy, making bodily generation a possible analogue for intellectual emergence.

surprising_valid_outliers.reader_inference: Both lexical scopes and the bracketed sequence are supplied. Their cross-domain connection and the receiving/bringing-forth analogy are mine. Ordinary recitation fully accounts for the imperative; the womb scope belongs to other attested constructions and does not establish deliberate wordplay here.
surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Surprising because a reproductive animal usage echoes a reading command; anchored by the intervening ʿalaq origin and teaching sequence. Retain only as a speculative resonance, never translate iqraʾ as conceive or assert a reproductive hidden meaning.

surprising_valid_outliers.reading: Alongside modest material origin, ʿalaq can acquire a countervailing resonance of something precious and cherished under the next verse's declaration of the Lord's generosity.

focus_anchor.role: The inventory includes a precious-object branch alongside the ordinary blood and attachment scopes.

activation_trace.role: A closely guarded precious object supplies value rather than mere smallness or low origin.
Nobility, generosity, and honoring make the value resonance locally available.

structural_cues.role: The material origin remains the primary construction.
The creator is immediately characterized by supreme generosity.

surprising_valid_outliers.mechanism: Contextual generosity activates the cherished-object side of attachment as a possible evaluative undertone, resisting an inference that a modest biological origin makes its product worthless.

changed_reading.before: ʿAlaq foregrounds material smallness or dependence.
changed_reading.after: Its inventory also permits an exploratory resonance of preciousness under generous creation, coexisting with dependence.

surprising_valid_outliers.reader_inference: The two lexical scopes are supplied. Applying cherishedness to the created human is my inference; akram predicates the Lord, not explicitly the human, and the precious-object noun sense is not established by this vocalized construction.
surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Surprising because it reverses the valuation often attached to a lowly origin. Keep it a secondary resonance, not a translation from precious objects or proof that this particular branch is intended.

surprising_valid_outliers.reading: The later transgression image may cast the human from thick blood as a being whose self-inflation resembles blood or water exceeding its bounds.

focus_anchor.role: The ordinary blood-material reading provides a physical image that later excess can transform.

activation_trace.role: Thick or congealed blood supplies the material starting image.
Overflowing water and blood, as forces exceeding measure, offer a physical analogue for transgression.

structural_cues.role: The human category begins with a bodily material.
The repeated human category carries the excess verb.
Self-assessed sufficiency supplies the stated behavioral connection, limiting the physical analogy.

surprising_valid_outliers.mechanism: Repetition of the human subject connects an early compact blood image to a later lexical image of material exceeding bounds, giving the moral reversal a possible physical texture.

changed_reading.before: Blood names the human's material beginning.
changed_reading.after: That material image can also make later overstepping imaginable as a bounded beginning becoming excessive.

surprising_valid_outliers.reader_inference: The blood scopes are supplied on both roots. Their transformation into a compact-to-overflow analogy is mine; the text attributes transgression to self-perceived sufficiency, not to blood or bodily maturation.
surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Surprising because it crosses biological origin with moral excess, but anchored by the repeated human and the specific shared blood imagery. Do not present a physiological cause, a literal flood, or a second lexical translation of the verse.

summary.ordinary_reading: The Lord created humanity from ʿalaq, understood primarily as clotted or adhering generative material. The surrounding verses identify that creator with the Lord who commands reading and teaches humanity.
coexisting_readings: An exploratory attachment image gives the material origin a relational contour of dependence.
Creation and teaching present received bodily and cognitive capacities; later self-sufficiency and return make the origin a corrective to human presumption.

The worship conflict allows a more exploratory reading in which common created status undercuts the prohibitor's authority, and bodily seizure versus prostration enacts opposing responses to dependence.
Secondary exploratory resonances include a reproductive echo around reading, preciousness alongside modest origin, and a blood-to-overflow analogy for later transgression.
unresolved_limits: The packet records no source gaps and supplies all nineteen ayat in the window. Available inventories are possibilities, not evidence that every branch is intended at its occurrence.
The focus does not specify modern anatomical stages, an external historical identity, or a causal biology of transgression.
Material or collective blood, attachment, and conception overlap without resolving every lexical nuance of ʿalaq. The ordinary generative reading remains sufficient.

The social, embodied, and branch-distant readings depend on stated reader analogies. In particular, preciousness and reproductive recitation imagery cannot replace the actual constructions or be promoted to certain wordplay.
